[Bass Sequencer Intro]

[Verse 1]
Quarters click into the tray,
dryer twelve hums out of time.
You toss a sheet, it catches air,
I catch the corner, count to five.

[Pre-Chorus]
The buzzer stops, the room goes quiet,
I reach to fix your collar — don't.

[Chorus 1]
You fold, I'll pin the corners,
we step in close and then we don't,
the sheet folds small between our shoulders,
and neither one of us says so.

[Bell Break]

[Verse 2]
The dryer window shows two shapes,
spinning circles, side by side.
A stranger's radio plays a jingle,
you hum along, I lose the words.

[Pre-Chorus]
The dial clicks over to cool-down,
my thumb finds yours and slides off first.

[Chorus 2]
You fold, I'll pin the corners,
your sleeve brushes past and stays,
the sheet goes soft between our shoulders,
and neither one of us gives it away.

[Chorus 3 - Stripped]
You fold, I'll pin the corners,
that's as far as our arms will go.

[Chorus 3 - Full]
You fold, I'll pin the corners,
we pull it tight, the whole room sways,
the sheet comes clean between our shoulders,
and everything we don't say folds too.

[Outro]
One more fold. The sign blinks twice.

a screen door swinging on a hinge it forgot to close,
the second stair creaking under no one's weight,
the way it always did, the way it does now.

Nothing moving, nothing missing,
just the hush that fills a room
after somebody almost spoke,
a quiet wearing a shape it kept.

[Verse 2]

the screen door swinging shut now, not open,
the third stair creaking, not the second,
and I never went back to ask which one.

[Chorus 2]
Nothing moving, nothing missing,
just the hush that fills a room
before somebody almost speaks,
I can't say if it's tonight or that one.

one bead, unhurried, finding the step,

it's carrying a sound before it happens.

Something moving, something kept,
the cup I set out anyway, for two,
the porch dark, the door left unlatched,
a house half-listening for a knock that isn't coming.

[Long Fade]
the second stair, or maybe the third,
creaking under no one's weight.

[Verse 1]
Rented cuff riding up my wrist,
a plastic cup sweating in my grip,
the sconces dim when the band counts off,
a suit borrowed, its crease not mine to keep.
She's laughing blue by the bridesmaid's shoulder,
her voice carries over the cello,
the way it used to carry smaller rooms.
Her sister's eyes find mine and stall,
a glass tipped toward the edge of a table.

[Chorus 1]
Past the envelopes stacked on the gift table,
I take the long way round the floor.

[Guitar Break]

[Verse 2]
Palm wiped once against my thigh,
a photograph faded soft along the corner.
She's tucked toward the joke, doesn't clock me yet,
I let the room stay slow so she can watch me come.
Three years wore the crease into that picture,
nothing else about her moved this much.

[Chorus 2]
Close enough to smell the pressed flowers,
I take the long way round the floor.

[Bridge]
Fingers first, no word before it,
her laugh cuts soft in the middle, unfinished.
Her palm already knows the seam of my knuckles,
her mouth catching up a beat behind.

[Chorus 3]
Twenty feet folding into nothing between us,
I take the long way round the floor.

[Long Fade Vamp]
I take the long way round the floor.
Fingers first, the rest can wait.
Slow enough for her to see me coming.

Fog on the glass, I clear it with my sleeve,
One carton, tilted on the shelf between.

Knuckles stop an inch from yours, cold off your skin,
Bulb hums once, settles back to bright.

I tilt my head, eyes on the carton, not your face,

[Chorus 1]
Under the buzzing glow, I gotta ask you,

[Verse 2]
Sign out front's short one letter, dimmer,
Coat's a different color, buttoned to your chin.
Six months since I traced the freckles on your wrist,
An inch of cold air is all that's left between.

[Pre-Chorus]
Same tilt, eyes back on the carton again,
Testing my voice slow, quieter than before.

[Chorus 2]
Quiet months between us, I gotta ask you,
Have you been okay,
Bad wheel ticking closer, neither palm pulls away.

[String Break]
Bell chimes twice, the wheel ticks slow.

[Chorus 3]
Buzzing glow above us settling steady,
Have you been okay,
Fingers on the carton, we lift it together,
Neither palm pulls away.

[Outro]
Bell above the door, two notes,
One carton, nothing more.

She's already up the stairs in sock feet,
the television talking to an empty room.

finding her two mugs stacked handle to handle.

I don't say a word about it, haven't in years,
I just pull them loose and let the water run.

I set them mouth-first, spaced apart, angled
the way my mother taught me, years back.
Not a correction, the one thing I fix.

[Verse 2]
Upstairs the shower cuts on, the pipes complain,
I find the ring stuck to the bottom cup,
work it loose with the edge of my thumb,
ease the door shut so the latch stays quiet.

[Pre-Chorus]
I don't say a word about it, never have,
I wipe my palm dry on my shirt and wait.

I set them mouth-first, spaced apart, angled
the way my mother taught me, years back.

the way my mother taught me, years back.

a small rust of her morning at the rim.

Tomorrow two mugs will stack the same way again,
the same quiet chore we've kept for all these years.

She leaves the list under the pineapple magnet,
eggs, spinach, the dry cleaning slip.

her letters tilting left by the third line.

I check my watch, take the keys from the bowl,
eleven minutes along Pacific Coast Highway,
straight to the yellow-capped bottle she won't admit she wants.

[Chorus 2]
I set it front and center on the middle shelf,
so she sees it first when the door swings open.
I don't ask why her writing shrinks.
I just drive the eleven minutes instead.

[Verse 2]
Her car pulls into the carport twenty minutes after,
the radio low on the counter.
Two glasses wait on the spot the mail forgets,
ice cracking its same three cracks.

[Instrumental Break]

[Chorus 3]
I pour her cranberry over ice the way she takes it,
and slide the cold glass across to her stool.
Neither of us mentions the clinic.
Tomorrow the magnet keeps a shorter list.

[Fade Outro]
Eggs, spinach, the dry cleaning, the same three words,
and the juice cold by the time she's home.

and a door eased shut so it won't rattle.

tomorrow the same coffee, the same wooden spoon.

[Bass Intro]

[Verse 1]
Two piles on the counter,
his stack, then mine.
A catalog he ordered,
never mailed back.
I square the flyers into edges,
line them up by size.

[Pre-Chorus]
One envelope keeps sliding,
I set it aside.
The tape peels a small rip
along the side.

[Chorus 1]
His pile stacked by the window,
mine beside the door.
The card under the mailbox
keeps both our names.
I've sorted every letter,
I haven't changed that one.

[Verse 2]
Alone I skip the coffee,
straight to the crate.
The neighbor waves good morning,
I wave back and wait
until the door clicks shut behind me,
then my shoulders drop.

[Pre-Chorus]
An old envelope slides loose,
his ink slanted on the front.
Ten years back, my maiden name,
a stamp faded to dust.

[Chorus 2]
His pile stacked by the window,
mine beside the door.
So I kept two piles standing,
he used to leave me more.
Notes tucked under coffee cups
before the world knew our address.

[Sax Solo]

[Chorus 3]
His pile by the window,
mine beside the door,
tonight I let them touch,
just at the edge.

[Long Fade]

lyrics_rendered:
[String Intro]

[Chorus 1]
I stand at the counter, phone against my ear.
The kettle keeps boiling, I don't shut it off.
Two names on one card, one shared code.
I practice the sentence: cancel it.

[Verse 1]
I take the folder out from under the mail.
I tell my sister: only paperwork, nothing more.
I circle the number before I lose my nerve.
The kitchen clock counts every second twice.

[Chorus 2]
The line hums the same phrase, on and on.
A voice breaks in, warm and rehearsed.
He asks about the classes we signed up for in June.
I fold a towel and wait for a gap to say it.

[Verse 2]
He lists the months, the miles, the progress chart.
Says think of all we built, don't let it slip.
I wipe the counter while he keeps talking.
His key fob sits untouched on my ring.

[Piano Break]

[Chorus 3]
The music fades, his pitch climbs to a peak.
I set the towel aside and say it flat: cancel it.
The line goes quiet, then a click, then done.
I breathe out slow, set the phone on the counter.

[Outro]
The account closes; his key fob stays on my ring.

[Brush Intro]

[Verse 1]
The leaf on the sill
curls in on itself now.
Three days, maybe four —
I count them in cracked, dry soil.

[Chorus]
He always meant to.
A cup by the window, never filled.
My voice stays even on the phone,
just standing by the counter,
the cup warm in my palm.

[Verse 2]
I water the ferns first,
the ones that were mine.
This one waits its share,
a name he forgets to call twice.

[Chorus]
He always meant to.
A cup by the window, half spilled.
I'm not asking why now,
just tipping it slow,
letting the dirt take its fill.

[Instrumental Break]

[Bridge]
And the leaf lifts,
small, under my palm,
certain now
water is coming.
Forgetting a thing
isn't the same
as never loving it.

[Chorus 3]
He always meant to.
So I'll finish what he never did—
one cup, on the sill,
green again by morning.

[Ritard Outro]

[Rubato Intro]
A claim slip curls in my coat pocket,
both our names pressed under one blue line.

[Verse 1]
I count out exact change, no comment.
My collar sits straight, my voice steady—
one line left open on the ledger.

[Chorus 1]
I hang the bag on the doorknob,
steam and his cologne caught in the wool.
One small errand left tonight:
call the cleaners, strike his name.
I keep not doing it.

[String Break]

[Verse 2]
The kettle clicks off twice
before I remember why I filled it.
His writing circles the pickup date.

[Chorus 2]
I hang the bag on the doorknob,
brush the lint where his sleeve used to rest.
One small errand left tonight:
call the cleaners, strike his name.
I keep not doing it.

[Bridge]
Both our names ride the same small ticket.
Nobody's crossed a single letter,
some foolish part of me was hoping no one would.

[Chorus 3 - lifted]
I fold the claim slip into my wallet,
skip the call, keep the reason mine.
Two names, one line, as long as they let it stay.
I keep not doing it.

[Outro]
I leave the tag on, just in case.

[Rhodes Intro]

[Verse 1]
A coffee ring, a brown moon on the table.
The fridge hums low, the only voice tonight.
I trace the crack that wanders cross the ceiling,
watch the minutes fall like dust in light.

[Pre-Chorus]
The streetlight leans in slow between the blinds,
soft as a palm still settling on mine.

[Chorus 1]
The quiet isn't empty,
it's leaning warm against the door.
Silence used to hollow out the floor,
now it curls up close, and nothing more.

[Verse 2]
Your sweater's folded on the chair, still holding
cedar, and rain, and somewhere caught in you.
I set two cups out when the kettle whistles,
pour the second one from habit, slow.

[Chorus 2]
The quiet isn't empty,
it's leaning warm against the door.
Silence used to hollow out the floor,
now it curls up close, and nothing more.

[Sax Interlude]

[Bridge]
Maybe grief's just love with nowhere left to go,
pooling in the hallway, soft and slow.

[Chorus 3]
The quiet isn't empty,
it's leaning warm against the door.
Silence used to hollow out the floor,
now it curls up close, and nothing more.

[Rhodes Outro]

Clocked off the dock, half past six,
silver warm from the wages till,
you round the corner, brolly blooming.

[Pre-Chorus]
Rain on the tarmac, rain on the crane,
one grey sheet stitched over our names.

[Chorus 1]
Under this umbrella, I'm not letting go,
the reel's in my ribs, gutters overflow,
step for step down Cable Street, chasing the gleam,
crook of your arm, the brolly pulled tight.

[Bodhran Drum Break]

[Verse 2]
Backroom fiddler counts the reel twice,
sawdust and stout swim round the till,
your boots on my boots, no room to fall.

[Pre-Chorus]
Rain on the cobbles, rain on the sign,
wet neon bleeds your name into mine.

[Chorus 2]
Under this umbrella, I'm not letting go,
fiddle's in the floorboards, gutters overflow,
one panel of nylon, collars turned high,
storm can take the wet night instead.

[Bridge]
Two coats, one spine, one collapsing dome,
whistle wound tighter, fiddle string blown,
count the shift, the fare, the miles thrown
into this narrow stretch of borrowed home.

[Chorus 3]
Under this umbrella, I'm not letting go,
the reel's in my ribs, gutters overflow,
step for step down Cable Street, chasing the gleam,
crook of your arm, the brolly pulled tight.

[Celtic Pipe Outro]

and I'm banging on nobody's door but yours.

[clear female vocal lead singing, f dynamic, bright, displaced]

[female lead with a female voice a third above, f dynamic, bright, displaced]

Flashlight on, no bulb up above
Bands snap off two stacks, gone quiet

[Chorus 1]
Count it, count it, thumb turns white
Mirror on the door, not the light
Count it, count it, don't look twice
Eleven down, the lot stays bright

[Verse 1]
Bands curl on the glass, a shed snake's skin
Ice on my wrist sparks off the mirror,
angled to catch whoever's coming in
Feed calls me family, tags me in the flex
but the cousin on the couch's the only name
that counts if the door swings loose
Bill pinched white, splitting who's owed, close

[Chorus 2]
Count it, count it, thumb turns white
Mirror on the door, not the light
Count it, count it, don't look twice
Eleven down, the lot stays bright

[Verse 2]
Phone buzzing face-down, her name lit up
come out, we celebrating, I let it ring
Ice used to flex, now it points a line
straight to my wrist under the stoop lamp
Keys jingle by the door, cousin shifts
hand freezes on a hundred, splits the cut
Online they're all mine, in here it's just blood I know

[Bridge]
Two stacks, one door, one mirror watching
nobody past the glass claims this weight

[Chorus 3]
Count it, count it, thumb turns white
Mirror on the door, not the light
Count it, count it, don't look twice
Eleven down, the lot stays bright

[Outro]
Bands snap again, the glass goes quiet
flashlight off, the door stays shut

lyrics_rendered:
[Pitched Vocal Intro]
Ring, ring, the floorboards catch the buzz
I don't say hello, I just breathe into the hum

[Verse 1]
Two buzzes on the floorboards, blinds not open yet
Voice comes out cracked, half a laugh, half a plea
I know, I know, don't say it, that's all it takes for me
Sitting up already, bare feet on the tile
Yesterday's shirt on the doorknob

[Pre-Chorus]
Ice cubes clink on your end of the line
Glass sweats a ring onto skin I can see too clear
Neither one says the address out loud

[Chorus]
Ring, ring, I'm already dressed
Ring, ring, chasing the same old mess
Keys in my fist, phone hot on my cheek
Ring, ring, the one thing giving my pulse a beat

[Drop]
Third ring, I'm moving
Stairs, two at once
Job never wired me up, gym never did
Static at 3am, and it's fixed

[Verse 2]
No Tuesday on the other end of that call
No morning, no gray, no nine o'clock at all
Just ice and your breath, a bare thigh I'm picturing
Proof, for a minute, my chest is really working

[Chorus]
Ring, ring, I'm already dressed
Ring, ring, chasing the same old mess
Keys in my fist, phone hot on my cheek
Ring, ring, the one thing giving my pulse a beat

[Chorus]
Ring, ring, I never learn
Ring, ring, the only pulse I chase

[Long Tail]
Stairwell door swinging shut behind me
Address known, phone finally quiet
Tuesday waits gray behind the blinds

[Musical Saw Intro]

[Verse 1]
[hot male vocal lead singing, mf dynamic, hot, petty]
A ladder up the wall.
He is rolling on the green I asked for.
I asked at fourteen. Again at nineteen.
Both times: a lot of green.
He is doing it anyway.
The paint smells louder than the street.
I have stopped walking, and I do not hide it.

[Chorus 1]
[male lead with a male voice a fourth above, f dynamic, hot, petty]
My color. Their house. And it looks good.
Exactly as good as I said it would.
I want to climb up and take the credit
for an idea nobody remembers refusing.

[Verse 2]
[hot male vocal lead singing, mf dynamic, hot, petty]
A kid puts a hand on the wet wall.
He gets told off. The print stays.
That is his now. The green is his.
The whole front of it belongs to him.
It took thirty years to win that.
He would not care. Rightly.
The radio on the ladder is fine.

[Chorus 2]
[male lead with a male voice a fourth above, f dynamic, hot, petty]
My color. Their house. And it looks good.
Exactly as good as I said it would.
The handprint is the best part of it
and I did not think of the handprint.

[Musical Saw Interlude]

[Bridge]
[hot male vocal lead singing, p dynamic, hot, petty]
The wish was granted to a stranger.
Nobody owes me the moment where I am right.
I have waited for it
since I was fourteen.
Better than fine. That is the cost.

[Chorus 3]
[male lead with a male voice a fourth above, ff dynamic, hot, petty]
My color. Their house. I keep walking.
Exactly as good as I said it would.
The man on the ladder does not turn.
Thirty years to be right about a green.
Being right took two seconds.

[Musical Saw Fading Outro]

Gold cursive card, sparkler wax dripping slow

[808 Slide Intro]

[Verse 1]
Three dollars in quarters, breath white off the block
Sixty-three rolls past, won't slow, won't stop
Driver clocks a fare, not a face, not a name
Tre leans on the turnstile, phone tucked in a shoe
Eight seconds on loop, living in my chest
Every fist reopens what the last one broke

[Chorus 1]
Past, past, watch it blow past
Ain't no seat for a kid at the glass
Past, past, watch it blow past
Counting quarters that don't add to a pass

[Verse 2]
Bus brakes for somebody else, doors hiss open
I clock the exact cold of that ride pulling off
Memorize the temperature, tuck it inside
That corner, that freeze, that static in a shoe
Wrote the first verse before I owned a pen

[Chorus 2]
Past, past, watch it blow past
Ain't no seat for a kid at the glass
Past, past, watch it blow past
I remember that cold, calling it my compass

금요일 밤 열한 시에 다 무너졌어
회사에서 잘렸고 연인도 떠났고
월세 밀린 고지서가 식탁 위에

전화를 걸었어 말이 안 나왔어

아무 말도 못하는 밤에
끊기지 않는 전화 하나가

[Chorus 1]
같이 울어줄 사람이 있다는 것
혼자 울 수 있는 게 강한 거라 했는데
진짜 강한 건 네 앞에서
무너질 수 있는 이 용기였어

[Verse 2]
고등학교 때 기억나
네가 옥상에서 울고 있었잖아
나는 그냥 옆에 앉았어
아무 말 없이 같이 하늘 봤어
한참 뒤에 내가 그랬지
야 밥 먹으러 가자
지금 이 전화가 그때랑 똑같아
침묵인데 연결돼 있어
숨소리의 리듬이 맞아가
네 호흡이 내 호흡을 잡아줘

[Pre-Chorus 2]
말이 닿지 않는 밤에
숨소리만으로 충분했어
그게 얼마나 큰 건지

[Chorus 2]
같이 울어줄 사람이 있다는 것
세상에서 가장 작은 교회였어
전화기 하나로 만든
두 사람만의 새벽 예배

[Verse 3]
새벽 다섯 시 네가 말했어
야 나 지금 네 집 앞인데
한 시간을 달려온 너
편의점 봉지 들고 서 있었어
공원 벤치에 나란히 앉았어
삼각김밥 하나씩 들고
아무 말 없이 새벽 하늘 보다가
네가 그랬잖아
야 이거 기도 같다
그 말에 처음으로 웃었어

[Bridge]
말없이 옆에 있어주는 것
그게 가장 깊은 기도라는 걸
오늘 새벽에 알았어

[Climax Chorus]
같이 울어줄 사람이 있다는 것
이 세상에서 가장 거룩한 일
삼각김밥을 나눠 먹는 새벽
가장 낮은 곳에서의 가장 높은 기도
너 때문에 다시 아침이 왔어

[Outro]
통화시간 세 시간 사십칠 분
그게 내 첫 번째 기도였어
